title: MAME 0.34
subtitle: Nicola Salmoria and the MAME team, 1998 · 959 games, twelve CPU cores, ROMs found by CRC
argsHint: a game name plus MAME's own switches (-nosound, -vesa, -ror, -frameskip n, -list, -listfull, -listcrc). -nodouble is there because the release doubles small pictures in a VESA mode through two routines written in x86 assembly, which this build does not have; without it a game that would be doubled stops at its first frame.
fpsNote: A FALLBACK cap only: the program paces itself from drv->frames_per_second through the real clock.

needsData.hint: one zip per game, named after it (invaders.zip, 1942.zip), in a mame/ directory of the games directory. From 0.34 on MAME identifies a ROM inside the zip by its CRC, so the set has to be the one this release expects: `node tools/mame-audit.mjs --roms=<dir>` says which of yours are.

safepointsNote: MAME waits for a key to be RELEASED with `while (osd_key_pressed(k));`, and osd_key_pressed is the game's own C reading Allegro's key[] out of memory -- no call, so nothing outside the loop can see it or break it. The safepoint is where key[] gets refreshed, which is also what a real Allegro does from a keyboard interrupt.
_needsData: `dir` is the data ROOT, a directory served by `serve.mjs --games=<dir>`. `lazy` means the root is only LISTED: a ROM collection is thousands of zips and a run opens one or two (a clone opens its parent's), so each file is fetched when the program opens it. `under` keeps the listing to one subdirectory, so the loose files of an older MAME's sets beside it are not offered.
